content.text: OTC intravaginal options incl clotrimazole 1% cream 5 g daily for 7–14 days, miconazole 2% cream 5 g daily for 7 days, or miconazole 200 mg vaginal suppository for 3 days; Rx option: terconazole 0.4% cream 5 g daily for 7 days. Creams and suppositories are oil based and might weaken latex condoms and diaphragms. Severe VVC: 7–14 days of a topical azole (or fluconazole). Pregnancy: only topical azoles, applied for 7 days, are recommended. Topical agents USU cause no systemic SE (local burning or irritation might occur).

⍉ use if a vaginal yeast infection was never dx'd by a doctor; ask a doctor first if on warfarin (bleeding or bruising may occur); condoms and diaphragms may be damaged and fail to prevent preg or STDs; stop and see a doctor if Sx don't improve in 3 days or last > 7 days.
